title: SSDs, TRIM and forensics
quick: SSDs store data in flash and manage it themselves. With TRIM and garbage collection, deleted data can be erased by the drive, so recovery is less certain than on hard disks.

sections.title: How an SSD differs
text: A hard disk can overwrite a sector directly. Flash memory can only be written to empty pages, and it erases in whole blocks. The SSD controller therefore keeps its own map between the addresses the computer uses and the real flash locations.
It also moves data around for wear levelling, to spread wear, and for garbage collection, to free blocks. This happens inside the drive, without the operating system.

sections.title: What TRIM does
text: TRIM is a command with which the operating system tells the drive which blocks no longer hold used data. The drive may then erase them in the background. After that, reads of those areas can return zeros or other data, depending on the drive.
So a deleted file on an SSD with TRIM may disappear sooner than on a hard disk. Timing is not predictable and depends on the drive and firmware.

sections.title: What this means for examiners
text: Do not promise that deleted data can be recovered from an SSD. A write blocker still stops the computer writing, but it cannot stop the drive's own internal housekeeping once it has power.
Image the drive early, document the drive model and firmware, and note the file system and TRIM state if known. Carving and recovery results may be partial, and the report should say so.

compare.title: Hard disk and SSD after deletion
rows: May be erased by the drive
Can differ if the drive changes data itself

example: A laptop SSD is seized a week after a user deleted files. The examiner images it and finds the file records, but the data areas return zeros. The drive had run TRIM and cleanup, so the report notes that content could not be recovered.
mistakes: Expecting the same recovery rate as on a hard disk.
Believing a write blocker stops all changes inside an SSD.
Powering the drive on again and again before imaging.
Not recording drive model and firmware.

terms.meaning: Solid-state drive that stores data in flash memory.
A command telling the drive which blocks are no longer in use.
Drive housekeeping that erases unused flash blocks.
Spreading writes evenly over flash to extend its life.
The chip in the drive that manages flash and address mapping.

exam.q: Why is recovery on SSDs less predictable?
exam.a: The drive's controller can erase freed blocks by itself through TRIM and garbage collection, at times the examiner does not control.

exam.q: Does a write blocker make an SSD image fully stable?
exam.a: It stops writes from the computer. It does not stop the drive's own internal processes, so repeated images can differ.
